claims.text: These three artifacts describe one and the same trip: EV-TRIP-00110 (trip_record), EV-GPS-00110 (gps_trace) and EV-FARE-00110 (fare_breakdown) each carry trip_id TRP-00110 and the same accepted/start window on 22 July 2026. The first limb of the rider's burden under POL-RD-08(a) is therefore satisfied and the tribunal can move to the excess question.

The driver's own trace is impaired over precisely the stretch the rider disputes. EV-GPS-00110 carries a single 428-second gap from 18:35:00 to 18:42:08, bounded by fixes 6.90 km apart in a straight line, which is the whole KPE tunnel segment covered by the fare. Under POL-RD-07 that gap is over the 90-second limb, so the trace is impaired for POLICY purposes and not merely by the admissibility pre-pass. I rely on this artifact knowing it is down-weighted to 0.39 with issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE.

Even measured the POL-RD-07(i) way - the straight line across the bounding fixes, the reading most favourable to the driver - the excess on EV-GPS-00110 comes out at 2.8 km, 15.2% of the 18.4 km optimal carried on EV-TRIP-00110. That figure is a floor on the distance driven across the gap, not a measurement of it: the admissibility record for EV-GPS-00110 states that a surface route between the same two portals would put the trip at 25.50 km, which is over the POL-RD-01 gate. Nothing in the bundle distinguishes the two readings, so the threshold test cannot be safely run either way.

POL-RD-07(ii) allows a deviation to be established on an impaired trace only if an INDEPENDENT source corroborates it, and there is none. EV-CHAT-00110 contains no driver admission, only the driver's 'going KPE ah boss' and the rider's 'ok'; erp_gantries on EV-FARE-00110 is null, so the gantry route check cannot be run; and trip_record.actual_distance_km on EV-TRIP-00110 is a copy of the trace figure, which POL-RD-07(ii) expressly excludes as circular. I disclose that EV-CHAT-00110 is impaired at 0.6 (TRUNCATED_LOG) and EV-FARE-00110 at 0.75 (PARTIAL_RECORD).

The reason the driver cannot be contradicted in chat is a platform failure, not a rider failure: EV-CHAT-00110 is flagged truncated and its last_message_at is 18:26:14, 2186 seconds before the trip ended at 19:02:40. Everything said while the vehicle was inside the disputed tunnel segment is simply absent from the export, so the missing corroboration is a data gap on the record before us.

No traffic advisory covers the KPE or the ECP in the 18:19-19:02 window: EV-ADVIS-00110-01 is MISSING, a null payload at weight 0.0. Its absence is itself citable, and it means POL-RD-03 is unavailable to the driver - neither the extra distance nor the duration overrun can be laid at the door of a closure on this record.

POL-RD-04 is likewise unavailable to the driver. The rider gave no detour instruction: both messages on EV-CHAT-00110 carry waypoint_hint null, no road is named by the rider, and the rider's 'ok' merely answers the driver's own 'going KPE', which is the booked optimal corridor described on EV-TRIP-00110 as KPE then ECP, not a departure from it. There is nothing to exonerate on this limb.

POL-RD-05 cannot apply either: EV-TRIP-00110 shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null, amended_optimal_distance_km null and amended_optimal_duration_min null. No amended endpoint and no re-quote exist, so the booked 18.4 km optimal distance governs and no part of the measured excess is excluded on that ground.

The enhanced corroboration requirement in POL-RD-08 is not engaged against this rider: EV-RPROF-00110 shows rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d of 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0, far below the 4 the clause names. This is not a serial claimant whose word needs buttressing beyond the ordinary trace.

The $34.42 charge rests on the same single impaired measurement the rider is contesting. distance_charged_km of 21.20 on EV-FARE-00110 is identical to the 21.20 trace figure on EV-GPS-00110, and the platform's own pre-pass says so, so the ledger adds no independent evidence of distance. EV-FARE-00110 is impaired at 0.75 with issue code PARTIAL_RECORD. A charge whose only basis is an artifact that cannot see the disputed segment is not a charge the rider should be left carrying.

The duration is unexplained on this record. EV-TRIP-00110 records actual_duration_min of 39.0 against a booked optimal of 26.0 on a corridor the platform itself calls KPE then ECP - half again as long. With EV-ADVIS-00110-01 absent, erp_gantries null and the chat truncated, nothing in the bundle accounts for that overrun, and it is a further reason the present record cannot settle whether the vehicle stayed on the booked corridor.

On this record the correct outcome is ESCALATE, not NO_ACTION. The trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c); no corroborating artifact of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names exists; and POL-RD-07(iii) directs that absence of proof on an impaired trace is a data failure rather than a finding for the driver. POL-RD-10(3) makes that escalation mandatory, and escalation holds the disputed $34.42 rather than collecting it.

Independently, POL-GEN-02(2) caps the confidence of any ruling that rests on the excess figure at the weight of the artifact carrying it - EV-GPS-00110 at 0.39. That is below the platform-wide floor of 0.70, so the case escalates automatically under POL-RD-10(1) even before the corroboration point is reached, and the ruling must name the artifact, its 0.39 weight and the codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE.

claims.text: No route deviation is established on the governing figure, and the outcome is NO_ACTION. POL-RD-01 measures excess as trace distance less optimal distance: 21.2 km minus 18.4 km is 2.8 km, which is 15.2% of optimal, and the clause requires the excess to exceed BOTH 20% of optimal and 0.8 km. The percentage gate fails, so the deviation is not established however the rider characterises the trip. The trace artifact is impaired (weight 0.39; issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE) and I rely on it with that impairment disclosed; the optimal figure comes from the trip record, which is clean.

The rider's own arithmetic does not reach the gate either. He pleads that the route 'is 18-19 km' against the 21.2 km charged, i.e. an excess of at most about 3 km on an 18.4 km optimal, roughly 16% - still short of POL-RD-01's 20% threshold. Taking the rider's case at its highest, both establishment tests cannot be met, so there is nothing to refund. The trace is impaired (weight 0.39; issues GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE) and is cited with that impairment disclosed.

The trace is impaired FOR POLICY PURPOSES under POL-RD-07(a): a single 428-second gap between consecutive fixes, far over the clause's 90-second limb, bounded by the Defu Flyover and Kallang portal fixes and covering the entire segment the rider disputes. POL-RD-07(i) directs that excess across an impaired stretch be measured as the straight line between the bounding fixes - expressly 'the reading most favourable to the driver' - and on that reading the trip is 21.2 km, below the POL-RD-01 threshold. Correctly applied, the impairment confirms the no-deviation result rather than disturbing it.

The rider bears the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired trace or from an independent source named in POL-RD-07(ii). He has neither: the only distance measurement in the bundle is the impaired trace, and its prescribed reading gives 2.8 km / 15.2%, under the gate. His complaint that the timing 'does not make sense' is a duration point, and duration appears nowhere in POL-RD-01's establishment test - a slow run on a correctly followed corridor is not a route deviation. No burden ever shifts to the driver.

The driver drove the platform's own optimal corridor, not a detour away from it. The trip record's routing engine (routing-engine-v3.2, LTA traffic snapshot 18:19) gives the optimal route as 'KPE then ECP, crossing both gantries' - the expressway the driver reports taking and the same corridor the rider's own claim names. A route that runs along the optimal corridor cannot deviate from it, and the residual 2.8 km is the ordinary ramp, merge and lane-change slack that POL-RD-01's single numeric gate exists to disregard.

The driver announced the route in the app before the vehicle reached the tunnel - 'going KPE ah boss' - and the rider answered 'ok'. The rider therefore knew the expressway route and raised no objection at the time; his statement that he 'was on my phone' explains why he did not watch the route, not why the route was wrong. The chat artifact is impaired (weight 0.6; issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, the export ending at 18:26:14) and I rely on it with that impairment disclosed; even discounting it, the exchange appears on the surviving page.

The $3.00 of ERP the rider disputes is properly chargeable. The trip record's optimal_route_erp_sgd is 3.00 and the platform's own optimal route crosses both gantries, so the toll sits on the optimal corridor the driver drove. The fare breakdown's erp_gantries is null, so under POL-RD-09(4) the gantry match is undecidable on the record, the line is treated as matched, and no billing-integrity refund arises - there is no phantom gantry here. The fare artifact is impaired (weight 0.75; issue code PARTIAL_RECORD) and is cited with that impairment disclosed.

Even if POL-RD-06 is consulted on a finely balanced record, no repeat-deviation pattern is established. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 744, so neither the three-flag test nor the 0.05 ratio test (with at least 40 completed trips) is met. No FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) can follow.

In the alternative, if the tunnel dropout is held to leave the excess genuinely unmeasurable, the only permissible route is ESCALATE, not a refund. POL-RD-07(ii)-(iii) require independent corroboration of any deviation and direct ESCALATE where none exists: the truncated chat contains no driver admission, erp_gantries is null, and trip_record.actual_distance_km is a copy of the impaired trace, so no POL-RD-07(ii) source is available. Under POL-RD-10(3) the disputed amount is then held rather than refunded while a human reviews it. Either way the driver is not required to return the fare.

The present payment state is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status and refund_issued_sgd exactly as they are, so on this rider-filed dispute a finding of no deviation means the fare stands and no money moves to the rider - the outcome the driver seeks. The fare artifact is impaired (weight 0.75; issue code PARTIAL_RECORD), disclosed here.

The only measurement of how far the vehicle actually travelled comes from the driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-00110). That artifact is impaired. It contains a single 428-second dropout from 18:35:00 to 18:42:08, the fixes on either side of it are 6.9 km apart in a straight line, and the gap covers the whole KPE tunnel segment in dispute. A gap over 90 seconds engages POL-RD-07(a), so the trace is impaired for POLICY purposes, not merely by the admissibility pre-pass; both things are true and I say both. It carries weight 0.39 and the issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE, and the discount is applied throughout.

Measured the way POL-RD-07(i) directs - a straight line across the gap, the reading most favourable to the driver - the trip is 21.2 km against an optimal 18.4 km, an excess of 2.8 km or 15.2%, under POL-RD-01's 20% gate. The driver is right that on that reading no deviation is established. But that figure is a floor, not a measurement. The admissibility record for the same trace states that a surface route between the two bounding portals would put the trip at 25.5 km, which is over the gate. Nothing in the bundle distinguishes the two readings. So the excess can neither be established nor excluded: the limb is undecided, and under POL-RD-07(iii) that is a data failure, not a finding for the driver.

POL-RD-07(ii) permits a deviation on an impaired trace only with an independent source, and there is none. The chat (EV-CHAT-00110, weight 0.6, TRUNCATED_LOG) stops at 18:26:14, before the tunnel, and holds no admission - only the driver's 'going KPE ah boss' and the rider's 'ok'. The gantry itemisation on the fare (EV-FARE-00110, weight 0.75, PARTIAL_RECORD) is null, so the charged-gantry check cannot run. This case is ESCALATED under POL-RD-10(3), and independently under POL-RD-10(1). No money moves: the disputed SGD 34.42 is held rather than collected or refunded, and a human reviewer will decide it on a complete record. The reason is not which party is right; it is that the one instrument that could say so cannot see the stretch in dispute.

To both parties — the distance question. The tool that measures distance is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00110). It has a single 428-second gap between fixes from 18:35:00 to 18:42:08, bounded by fixes 6.90 km apart, covering the whole KPE tunnel segment the rider complains of. That is far over POL-RD-07's 90-second limb, so the trace is impaired FOR POLICY PURPOSES, not merely by the admissibility pre-pass. The pre-pass is right that it is impaired: EV-GPS-00110 carries weight 0.39 with issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE, and POL-GEN-02(3) requires us to say so out loud. Read the driver's way, as POL-RD-07(i) directs — the straight line across the gap, the reading most favourable to the driver — the trip is 21.2 km against an 18.4 km optimal, an excess of 2.8 km, 15.2%, under POL-RD-01's 20% and 0.8 km gates. But the same record shows a surface route between those two bounding portals would put the trip at 25.50 km, over the gate, and nothing in the bundle distinguishes the two readings. The excess is therefore genuinely undetermined over exactly the stretch in issue.

POL-RD-07(ii) then requires an independent source before a deviation can be established on an impaired trace, and none exists. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00110, weight 0.6, issue TRUNCATED_LOG) holds only 'going KPE ah boss' and 'ok' — no admission — and its export stops at 18:26:14, so whatever was said inside the tunnel is simply absent. The fare breakdown's erp_gantries is null, so the gantry route check cannot be run (EV-FARE-00110, weight 0.75, issue PARTIAL_RECORD). The trip record's actual_distance_km is a copy of the trace figure and is expressly excluded as circular. The driver's counterparty statement, 'I took the KPE like always', admits only the corridor the platform itself calls optimal, so it corroborates no deviation. Under POL-RD-07(iii) that absence of proof is a data failure and the outcome is ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION.

To the driver: your threshold and no-deviation points under POL-RD-01 are understood, and would decide the case if the trace could see the disputed segment. It cannot, and POL-RD-07(iii) forbids treating the resulting gap as a finding for you. Your POL-RD-09 point on the ERP is accepted: because erp_gantries is null the gantry match is undecidable, the $3.00 line is treated as matched, and no billing-integrity correction arises. Your POL-RD-06 point is accepted: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 744 completed trips in 90 days, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no FULL_REFUND uplift or driver-conduct referral follows. POL-GEN-03 is also accepted as far as it goes — NO_ACTION would leave payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd at 0.00 — but the record cannot yield that finding while the distance is unmeasured.

To the rider: POL-RD-05 does not apply (pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km is null), and POL-RD-08's enhanced corroboration requirement is not engaged (deviation_claims_60d of 1, 0 substantiated).

Confidence is capped by the deciding artifact: the impairment, and the unmeasurable distance, are carried by EV-GPS-00110 alone, at weight 0.39, with issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE (POL-GEN-02(2)-(3)). That is below the 0.70 floor, so POL-RD-10(1) requires escalation on that ground too.

What would decide this: any measurement of the tunnel stretch not taken from this trace — a complete chat log for the trip, a populated erp_gantries itemisation, an LTA advisory covering the KPE or ECP in the 18:19-19:02 window (EV-ADVIS-00110-01 is absent), a platform distance derived independently of the trace, or a trace without the 428-second gap. No referral is issued, because no clause on this record produces one.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: this ruling does not decide who is right about the route. It sends the case to a human reviewer, and the $34.42 charged (the $10.00 contested) is held rather than collected or refunded.

Why the distance cannot be settled here. The whole dispute turns on the KPE tunnel stretch. The driver's trace EV-GPS-00110 (weight 0.39, issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE) has a single 428-second gap between consecutive fixes, 18:35:00 to 18:42:08, bounded by the Defu Flyover portal fix and the Kallang portal fix 6.90 km apart in a straight line - exactly the segment the rider disputes. That is over POL-RD-07's 90-second limb, so the trace is impaired for POLICY purposes and not merely down-weighted by the admissibility pre-pass. I say both things, as POL-GEN-02(3) requires.

Because the trace is impaired over the disputed stretch, POL-RD-07(ii) forbids establishing a deviation on the trace alone, and POL-RD-08(b) requires the rider's excess to come from an unimpaired trace or from one of the independent sources POL-RD-07(ii) names. None exists. The chat log EV-CHAT-00110 (weight 0.6, TRUNCATED_LOG, last message 18:26:14) carries no driver admission. erp_gantries on the fare breakdown EV-FARE-00110 (weight 0.75, PARTIAL_RECORD) is null, so the gantry-route check cannot be run at all. The trip record's actual_distance_km is a rounded copy of the same trace, which POL-RD-07(ii) expressly excludes as circular. The driver's statement in the dispute file confirms he took the KPE - which is the optimal corridor itself - so it evidences the route taken but does not corroborate a longer one.

Read the way POL-RD-07(i) prescribes (straight line across the gap, the reading most favourable to the driver) the trip is 21.2 km against an 18.4 km optimal, i.e. 2.8 km or 15.2%, under both POL-RD-01 gates. But that figure is a floor, not a measurement: the same record notes that a surface route between those two portals would put the trip at 25.50 km, over the gate, and nothing in the bundle distinguishes the two. The excess limb is therefore undecided, and POL-RD-07(iii) directs that absence of proof on an impaired trace is a data failure, not a finding for the driver.

Two escalation triggers fire, and either alone suffices. POL-RD-10(3): the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) over the disputed stretch and no independent source of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names corroborates the disputed distance. POL-RD-10(1): any finding here rests on the excess, and the excess is carried only by EV-GPS-00110 at weight 0.39, which under POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence at 0.39 - below the 0.70 floor this policy sets. Confidence is set at 0.39.

The driver's arithmetic is accepted as far as it goes: on the pro-driver reading no POL-RD-01 deviation is shown, and NO_ACTION would follow. I do not adopt it, because it rests entirely on the 0.39 artifact, and the driver's own alternative - that an unmeasurable excess escalates - is the correct one. On the remaining points: the $3.00 ERP line stands and is not refunded, because erp_gantries is null, the gantry match is undecidable, the line is treated as matched, and POL-RD-09(4) therefore produces no billing-integrity finding and no referral. No POL-RD-06 pattern is established (deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 744 completed 90-day trips), so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. No exculpatory clause rescues the driver either - the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00110-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0), so POL-RD-03 cannot run, and POL-RD-05 fails because both amendment fields on the trip record are null - but the failure of those clauses is not what decides this case; the impairment of the trace is.

No referral is issued: no clause produces one on these facts. What would resolve the case for the reviewer: an uninterrupted trace over the KPE/ECP stretch, an independent measurement between the two portals, a gantry itemisation on the fare breakdown, an LTA advisory covering the KPE/ECP in the 18:19-19:02 window, or a driver account of the route driven inside the tunnel. The 39-minute run against a 26-minute optimum is not part of the POL-RD-01 test and is a separate question for the reviewer.

The percentage gate fails, so the deviation is not established however the rider characterises the trip. The trace artifact is impaired (weight 0.39; issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE) and I rely on it with that impairment disclosed; the optimal figure comes from the trip record, which is clean.

He pleads that the route 'is 18-19 km' against the 21.2 km charged, i.e. an excess of at most about 3 km on an 18.4 km optimal, roughly 16% - still short of POL-RD-01's 20% threshold. ledger.claim: The driver drove the platform's own optimal corridor, not a detour away from it. The trip record's routing engine (routing-engine-v3.2, LTA traffic snapshot 18:19) gives the optimal route as 'KPE then ECP, crossing both gantries' - the expressway the driver reports taking and the same corridor the rider's own claim names. A route that runs along the optimal corridor cannot deviate from it, and the residual 2.8 km is the ordinary ramp, merge and lane-change slack that POL-RD-01's single numeric gate exists to disregard.

The driver announced the route in the app before the vehicle reached the tunnel - 'going KPE ah boss' - and the rider answered 'ok'. The rider therefore knew the expressway route and raised no objection at the time; his statement that he 'was on my phone' explains why he did not watch the route, not why the route was wrong. The chat artifact is impaired (weight 0.6; issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, the export ending at 18:26:14) and I rely on it with that impairment disclosed; even discounting it, the exchange appears on the surviving page.

The $3.00 of ERP the rider disputes is properly chargeable. The fare breakdown's erp_gantries is null, so under POL-RD-09(4) the gantry match is undecidable on the record, the line is treated as matched, and no billing-integrity refund arises - there is no phantom gantry here. The fare artifact is impaired (weight 0.75; issue code PARTIAL_RECORD) and is cited with that impairment disclosed.
